Author: Gautam Chowdhary
Bench: Gautam Chowdhary
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 78 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 8382 of 2023 Applicant :- Kamal Sharma Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Amit Rai,Abhyudaya Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A for the State and perused the material on record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-Kamal Sharma for enlarging him on bail in Sessions Trial No. 95 of 2022, Case Crime No.750 of 2022 under Sections 498A, 304-B, 302,
120-B, 34 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station KOtwali City, District Bijnor.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is the husband of the deceased and the allegation against the applicant is that after the marriage, the applicant and his family members started making demand of dowry of Rs. 10 lacs as well as car, due to non-fulfilment of the same, the deceased was ousted from her matrimonial house in the month of January 2021 on account of which, a first information report was lodged in Case Crime No.696 of 2021 on 28.10.2021.On Kamal Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16018206/
1 29.10.2021 when the deceased was going to her college and when she reached near Saket Colony, the applicant along with his associates with an intention to kill her shot upon her, due to which she fell down and died.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that at the time of alleged incident, as per C.D.R. location, the applicant was Greater Noida, which itself falsifies the prosecution story.
He further submits that prior to one day of the alleged incident, a first information report was already lodged, therefore, it is unbelievable that the applicant would commit the offence again.
He next submits that except the confessional statement of the co-accused Raju Kashyap, there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant has hatched the conspiracy.
Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the applicant have also been placed before the Court.
The circumstances which, according to the counsel, led to the false implication of the accused have also been mentioned.

It has also been assured on behalf of the applicant that he is ready to cooperate with the process of law and shall faithfully make himself available before the court whenever required and is also ready to accept all the conditions which the Court may deem fit to impose upon him.
He next submits that applicant is languishing in jail since 25.11.2021 having no criminal history.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the applicant is the husband of the deceased and his innocence cannot be adjudged at pre trial stage,
therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence.
In case the applicant is released on bail he will misuse the liberty of bail.

Perusal of the record shows that the marriage between the applicant and the deceased was solemnised on 01.12.2017 and deceased died within a short span of four years of the marriage due to demand of dowry.

Furthermore, it is evident from the perusal of the statement of the co-accused Raju Kashyap, that the applicant has hired him to commit the murder of the deceased, thus the applicant is the conspirator of the alleged incident and therefore the applicant is not entitled for bail.

Keeping in view submissions of learned counsel for the parties, gravity of offence, nature of allegations and all the attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, no case for bail has been made out.
Accordingly, the bail application of applicant-Kamal Sharma is rejected.

Order Date :- 21.3.2023 S.Ali  Kamal Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16018206/
